text: Nothing for years, I never told anyone. When I was 20 I told a school counsellor at college, who was understanding. Mostly time helped.
Bisher noch nichts. Ich versuche, Polizei zu meiden.

Psychiatric treatment was essential: mood stabilisers (lamotrigine, which I still take), an antipsychotic for the first months, and regular check-ins with my psychiatrist. I started psychotherapy about two months after the episode, with a therapist who has experience with bipolar disorder and with psychedelic harms. We worked on shame and on rebuilding trust in my own perception.

Sleep hygiene has been huge. I now protect my sleep like nothing else. I've learned that sleep deprivation was a big part of what tipped me over at the retreat.

I wrote a detailed complaint to the retreat organisers, which they never answered. That was frustrating. I also posted a review describing what happened, and several people contacted me with similar stories, which helped me feel less alone.

My partner has been incredibly supportive and came to some therapy sessions.

I'm much better now. My mood is stable. But I still have moments where I don't trust a good mood, and I'll probably always be cautious.
I talked to my GP who reassured me and checked my blood pressure regularly for a while. CBT for health anxiety helped me stop checking all the time. I stopped experimenting with DIY brews completely.

Ich habe die Ketamin-Behandlung abgebrochen und bin zu einem anderen Psychiater gegangen, der mich ernst genommen hat. Ich habe ein anderes Antidepressivum bekommen und war sechs Wochen in einer Tagesklinik. Das hat mir etwas Stabilität gegeben. Die Depersonalisation ist inzwischen weniger geworden, aber noch da. Am wenigsten hilfreich war die Reaktion der ersten Klinik, die gesagt hat, so etwas sei 'nicht möglich' bei Ketamin.
Mostly talking about it with friends, and writing about it. I volunteer at a soup kitchen now.

I saw a neurologist for tests and talked to my psychiatrist, who was very clear that I must never combine psychedelics with lithium. I stayed on lithium. A few therapy sessions helped with the fear of seizures. It's gotten better with time.
Mit einer Freundin darüber geredet. Ging dann von selbst weg.

I resisted getting help for months because I felt I didn't deserve it, J was the one who'd been in hospital. My partner eventually insisted. My GP referred me to a trauma therapist, and after a long wait I started trauma-focused CBT, and later EMDR. EMDR made the biggest difference for the flashbacks. The lake images are still there but they don't hit me with the same force.

I was prescribed sertraline, which helped with the depression a bit, and prazosin for nightmares, which helped a lot.

I had a few conversations with J over the past year. It helped to hear him say that he didn't blame me and that he was grateful I went in after him. It helped less that he didn't remember most of it.

I've slowly been doing exposure on my own: first looking at photos of lakes, then walking along a river, then dipping my feet in the sea last summer. I'm planning to swim again this year.

Unhelpful: people in psychedelic communities online telling me this was a 'spiritual emergency' and that I should do another trip to 'integrate' it. I did not want that.
Rest, food and some talks with my partner. I'm wary of retreats now.

Ich habe nach etwa einem Jahr eine Traumatherapie begonnen. Am Anfang war es schwer, darüber zu sprechen, weil ich mich so geschämt habe. Die Therapie hat mir geholfen, die Panikattacken zu verringern und wieder in Menschenmengen zu gehen. Was mir auch geholfen hat, war Sport, vor allem Boxen, weil ich mich dadurch stärker und weniger hilflos fühle. Ich habe immer noch manchmal Angst, wenn ich Uniformen sehe.
